title: Evals Are Not Unit Tests — Ido Pesok, Vercel v0
talk_summary: Ido Pesok argues that application-layer evals, not unit tests, are how you make LLM features reliable, using a 'basketball court' model of data (in-domain prompts), tasks (the code/prompt under test), and simple pass/fail scores. He recommends collecting real user queries, factoring constants (data) from variables (system prompt/RAG), sharing the exact production code path with evals, and running evals in CI to catch regressions per PR.

takeaways.technique: Court model: data vs task separation
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep user queries as fixed 'data' constants and put the thing under test (system prompt, RAG, preprocessing) in the 'task', so changing a prompt doesn't require rebuilding the dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: put constants in data variables in the task... you want to factor constants so it improves clarity, reuse, and generalizations

takeaways.technique: Evals in CI with per-PR regression report
takeaways.what_they_do: They run the eval task across all data in CI and produce a report showing improvements and regressions per PR, so a prompt change that fixes one area but breaks another is visible before merge.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic pass/fail scoring over fuzzy scores
takeaways.what_they_do: They lean toward deterministic, pass/fail checks and ask 'what am I looking for to see if this failed?' rather than overengineered scoring, so results are debuggable and shareable across teams.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to actually lean towards deterministic scoring and pass fail... Keep your scores as simple as possible

takeaways.technique: Collect real failure cases from logs/feedback
takeaways.what_they_do: They harvest eval data from thumbs up/down, random log samples reviewed weekly, community forums, and social reports, and explicitly avoid out-of-domain prompts users never ask.

takeaways.technique: Eval-only output tags for easy scoring
takeaways.what_they_do: They add a small instruction (e.g. wrap final answer in tags) only in the eval prompt to make string-matching scoring trivial, while production prompts stay clean.

takeaways.technique: Share exact code path between eval and production
takeaways.what_they_do: They use AI SDK middleware so preprocessing/RAG/system prompt logic is shared between the real API route and the evals, making practice match the real game.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to share the pretty much the exact same code between evals and what you're actually running
